english: Let $S=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{7}\cos^{-1}\left(\sin\dfrac{2k\pi}{9}\right)$, where $\cos^{-1}$ takes values in $[0,\pi]$. Then the value of $\dfrac{180S}{\pi}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $S=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{7}\cos^{-1}\left(\sin\dfrac{2k\pi}{9}\right)$ है, जहाँ $\cos^{-1}$ के मान $[0,\pi]$ में हैं। तब $\dfrac{180S}{\pi}$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: For $y\in[-1,1]$, $\sin^{-1}y+\cos^{-1}y=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Hence each term is $\cos^{-1}(\sin\theta_{k})=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\sin^{-1}(\sin\theta_{k})$ with $\theta_{k}=\dfrac{2k\pi}{9}$, and $S=\dfrac{7\pi}{2}-\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{7}\sin^{-1}(\sin\theta_{k})$.

Work in degrees: $\theta_{k}=40k^{\circ}$, i.e. $40^{\circ},80^{\circ},120^{\circ},160^{\circ},200^{\circ},240^{\circ},280^{\circ}$. The value $\sin^{-1}(\sin\theta)$ is the unique angle in $[-90^{\circ},90^{\circ}]$ with the same sine.

$40^{\circ}$ and $80^{\circ}$ are already in range. For $120^{\circ},160^{\circ},200^{\circ},240^{\circ}$ use $\sin\theta=\sin(180^{\circ}-\theta)$: $60^{\circ},20^{\circ},-20^{\circ},-60^{\circ}$, all in range. For $280^{\circ}$ use $\sin\theta=\sin(\theta-360^{\circ})$: $-80^{\circ}$.

So, in degrees, $S=7\cdot90^{\circ}-40^{\circ}=590^{\circ}$, i.e. $\dfrac{180S}{\pi}=590$. As a check, the individual terms are $50,10,30,70,110,150,170$ degrees, each in $[0^{\circ},180^{\circ}]$, with sum $590$.
originality_note: New: a sum of cos^-1 of sines at the ninth-roots angles 40k degrees, reduced by cos^-1 = pi/2 - sin^-1 and the reflection of each angle into [-90,90]; the near-cancellation of the sin^-1 values leaves 40 degrees (way 5). Closest known: single evaluations such as cos^-1(sin(-5pi/6)). Different because: seven reductions in different quadrants must be summed, and the cancellation pattern is incomplete.

concept_use.Evaluation of inverse trigonometric expr: Each cos^-1(sin(40k degrees)) is evaluated to a principal value (50,10,30,70,110,150,170 degrees) and summed.
concept_use.Properties of Inverse trigonometric func: cos^-1 y = pi/2 - sin^-1 y and sin^-1(sin theta) = 180 - theta or theta - 360 in the right quadrant reduce every term.

key_step: Converting cos^-1(sin theta) to pi/2 - sin^-1(sin theta) and reducing seven angles into [-90,90] degrees.
justification: Several routine principal-value reductions chained with the complementary-angle property; precision risk is small. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q4 (L2) principal-value evaluation with range shifts.
